title: Nanzan
capsule: Nanzan (南山) was one of three competing kingdoms of the Sanzan period on Okinawa Island, controlling the southern portion of the island with its seat at Ōzato from 1314 until 1429. It maintained tributary relations with Ming China, dispatching at least 19 missions, and sustained itself through maritime trade with Southeast Asia and other Ryukyuan polities. The last king, Taromai, faced succession disputes that sapped the kingdom's cohesion, and in 1429 the Chūzan king Shō Hashi — having already absorbed Hokuzan in 1416 — conquered Nanzan, completing the unification of Okinawa into the Ryūkyū Kingdom. The attested dates in this dataset (1314–1402) reflect the Cliopatria source window rather than the full span of Nanzan's existence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Nanzan's control of southern Okinawa is broadly supported by chronicles and tribute records, but its internal boundaries with Chūzan and Hokuzan are not precisely delineated in surviving sources.
